doc.title: Sam Kininger interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clinton, New York, May 27, 2011

title: Modal thinking and transcribing
summary: Sam is somewhat modal; learning by listening and transcribing solos.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: Are you a mode thinker? Sometimes?

Somewhat yeah, I would say a modal player, yeah. Not so much the exact correct thinking, but I guess that coincides with what we were talking about before, like playing outside the key sort of but in it. Does that make sense? Now what’s a good example? But it would be, I think like that, yeah.
Sometimes the jazz scales that I see I feel like boy am I out of date. I don’t know what some of these things are. © Fillius Jazz Archive -20-

Yeah. Like not as much, but, I do a lot of listening, that’s what I do, and the transcribing is also a good thing. I used to just sit and try and learn solos, you know, learn people’s solos. I’m sure that’s still a pretty good means of learning your instrument, learning different styles.
